title: Recovery Supervisor, Admission Control & Durable Recovery Scheduling
supervisorAdmissionVerified: Durable discovery: listRecoverableReleaseIntents is the sole source of truth. No in-memory queue exists; a process restart rediscovers work from SQLite.
Bounded admission: runOnce caps execution to maxIntentsPerRun (default 50). Excess eligible intents are counted in report.deferredCapacity and left durable for the next cycle.
Lease-aware admission: live-leased intents are not executed by other workers; the executor counts lease contention via report.leaseHeld.
Single-owner admission: Phase 174 fenced transitions preserve single ownership even under concurrent supervisors.
Fairness: eligible intents are processed in listRecoverable's deterministic ordering; deferred work is picked up on subsequent cycles.
retryVerified: Durable retry state on release_deployment_intents: recovery_attempts, next_retry_at, last_failure_class.
Bounded backoff: next_retry_at = now + min(initialDelayMs * multiplier^(attempt-1), maxDelayMs) per retryPolicy.
Not-due intents are deferred at discovery: report.deferredNotDue counts them; no execution runs.
Exhaustion at maxAttempts: next_retry_at is set to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER so an exhausted intent is never rediscovered.
Audit: release.recovery.retry_scheduled on each scheduled retry, release.recovery.retry_exhausted at maxAttempts.
Storm protection: rapid repeated runOnce cycles cannot exceed maxAttempts for a given intent within the backoff window.
crashRestartVerified: Supervisor restart on the same SQLite file discovers prior recoverable intents.
RECOVERY_REQUIRED with providerStatus=UNKNOWN survives process restart unchanged.
A worker that lost its lease (crashed or superseded) is fenced by the Phase 174 atomic conditional transition; it cannot write terminal state after restart.
A new supervisor instance can claim expired leases and become the authoritative recovery owner.
auditBehaviorVerified: release.recovery.retry_scheduled / release.recovery.retry_exhausted emitted on the executor's audit sink.
release.recovery.started, release.recovery.advanced, release.recovery.lease.held, release.recovery.known_good, release.recovery.blocked (pre-existing) preserved.
release.recovery.supervisor.start / stop emitted on the supervisor's audit sink.
release.recovery.supervisor.started / stopped emitted on the event sink.
Audit is best-effort: failures cannot corrupt the state machine.
unknownOutcomeBehavior: Provider ambiguity is recorded as RECOVERY_REQUIRED with providerStatus=UNKNOWN.
UNKNOWN never becomes KNOWN_GOOD or FAILED without authoritative evidence.
RECOVERY_REQUIRED survives supervisor restart; retry bookkeeping is durable.
